title: Geometric short exact sequence for integral ideal patching
statement: Let $X$ be locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion with $Z$ integral [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $\xi$ have closure $i(Z)$. Let $P$ be any property of modules with $P(0)$, and suppose there is a coherent $G$ with support $i(Z)$ and $\mathfrak m_\xi G_\xi=0$ [def-weil-residue-field], such that for every quasi-coherent ideal inclusion $J\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ generically surjective at $\xi$, there is a coherent subobject $G^\prime\subseteq G$, factoring through $JG\hookrightarrow G$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk], generically surjective and satisfying $P(G^\prime)$. For each quasi-coherent ideal $I$ on $Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], there exist $r\ge1$ and a short exact sequence $H\to (i_*I)^{\oplus r}\to Q$ of coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent], with $i_*I$ coherent, together with a coherent $G^\prime$ with $P(G^\prime)$ and an isomorphism $H\cong G^\prime$. Moreover $\operatorname{Supp}(Q)\subseteq i(Z)$ and $Q_\xi=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. No extension closure, finite-sum descent or hypothesis asserting $P(Q)$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the property-independent geometric embedding lemma to the coherent G from the hypothesis and the chosen I. It supplies r≥1 and either a zero middle sum or an ideal inclusion ι:J→OX, generically surjective, with a mono τ:JG→M bijective at ξ.

Prove the ideal on Z coherent: closed immersion makes Z locally Noetherian; the structure sheaf is coherent, and the ideal is its quasi-coherent submodule. Quasi-coherence follows by applying affine pushforward to the structure sheaf of its closed subscheme, then taking the kernel of the structure-sheaf restriction. Finite pushforward proves i_*I coherent, and finite-sum closure proves M coherent.

Outside i(Z), every stalk of i_*I is zero by closed-pushforward stalks. Apply the additive underlying abelian-group stalk functor to the biproduct identity sum πjιj=id. All factors through these zero stalks vanish, so the identity on Mx is zero, and Mx is zero.

In the zero-middle case choose H=G prime=0 and use P(0). Otherwise apply the hypothesis on G to ι, obtaining coherent G prime satisfying P and h:G prime→JG with G prime.arrow=h followed by the ideal-product inclusion. Its composite is mono, so h is mono and f=hτ is mono. The ideal-product stalk inclusion is injective; cancel it against the generic surjectivity of G prime.arrow to prove hξ surjective. Compose with bijectivity of τξ to prove fξ surjective.

Take the canonical complex S=(H→M→coker f), which is short exact because f is mono. Its cokernel is coherent by coherent cokernel closure. Stalk exactness makes every stalk cokernel projection surjective. Outside i(Z) its source stalk is zero, so its target stalk is zero. At ξ every source element lifts through fξ, and the cokernel projection annihilates it; hence the cokernel stalk is again zero. Choose G prime=H and the identity isomorphism. The middle object is literally the specified biproduct.
